bull_bear.body: Regulatory risks, intense competition in the telecom sector
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: The credit rating upgrade may lead to lower borrowing costs for the company, improving its financial flexibility
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Debt from banks was reduced across the disclosed quarters from Rs 4,813 Cr (Q1FY25) to Rs 726 Cr (Q4FY26); NCDs were nil through Q2FY26 and stand at Rs 3,271 Cr (Q3FY26) and Rs 3,275 Cr (Q4FY26).
- Cash and cash equivalents were Rs 3,715 Cr at Q4FY26, versus Rs 9,932 Cr at Q4FY25 (as tabulated).
- Credit ratings improved to Crisil A-/Stable (May'26) and ICRA A- (Stable) (Jun'26); the deck cites 'Improved credit rating' as a positioning point.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Large subscriber base - over 198.5 Mn subscribers and 15.7% subscriber market share as of March 31, 2026 per TRAI subscription report; 192.8 Mn reported subscribers of which 128.9 Mn are 4G/5G
- Applicable Gross Revenue (ApGR) market share of 15.9% for the year ended March 31, 2026, with leading ApGR share in Mumbai and Kerala, second largest in Gujarat, and over 20% in Haryana, Kolkata, Maharashtra, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh (West)
- Competitive spectrum profile - 8,030.4 MHz total spectrum of which 8,012.8 MHz is liberalised and usable for any technology; mid-band 5G (3300 MHz) in 17 key service areas and mmWave 5G (26 GHz) in 16 service areas
- Highest 4G spectrum available per Mn subscribers, with sufficient capability to support migration of the entire 4G subscriber base to 5G
- Broad network reach - voice coverage of more than 1.2 bn Indians across over 487,000 census towns and villages; 4G broadband coverage over 414,500 census towns and villages covering close to 86% of population
- Parentage and promoter support from the Aditya Birla Group and Vodafone Group
- Digital ecosystem on the Vi app (Vi Movies & TV, Vi Finance, Vi Ads, Vi Games, Vi Shop, utility payments) that deepens engagement and customer stickiness
- Use of AI and data analytics for customer segmentation, targeted marketing, personalised recommendations and location-based services
- Credit rating upgraded to A- (Stable) by both CRISIL and ICRA during FY26
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer privacy and data security — BRSR material issue flagged as a Risk with negative financial implications. Rising privacy concerns over the use and sale of consumer data, heightened cybersecurity threats, and evolving Indian regulation under the DPDP Act. The Company states data security concerns can affect customer acquisition and retention, decrease market share and demand for VIL services, while data loss could cause non-compliance, legal ramifications and brand damage. Mitigations include licence-mandated confidentiality of subscriber information, alignment with DPDP Act requirements, regular customer privacy audits, minimised data retention and disciplinary action on breaches.
- Quality of network infrastructure and pace of technology upgrade — BRSR material issue flagged as a Risk with negative financial implications. Network infrastructure is vulnerable to technological failure from human error or natural disasters, and rapid technological advancement requires continuous upgrades to meet demand for stronger connectivity; failure to do so could adversely affect the business and market share. Mitigation is regular quality checks and recording complaint volumes. Scale of the service load is visible in the 4,770,473 customer complaints filed in FY 2025-26 with 7,961 pending at year close.
- Regulatory compliance — BRSR material issue flagged as a Risk. Failure to comply with regulatory requirements can lead to legal penalties, reputational damage and operational disruptions; the Company states it regularly monitors compliance to mitigate this and to build stakeholder trust.
- Climate change and climate-related regulation — BRSR material issue flagged as a Risk with negative financial implications. Emerging telecom-sector and global climate regulation (India's Net Zero 2070 commitment under UNFCCC/COP) focused on clean technologies and renewable energy, plus physical climate impacts on infrastructure - telecom disruptions threaten significant restructuring costs and hinder essential pre- and post-disaster communication. Mitigation is a structured climate governance framework and a designated Sustainability/ESG committee overseeing risks, mitigation and contingency plans.
- E-waste management — BRSR material issue flagged as a Risk with negative financial implications. Telecom and networking equipment contributes significantly to e-waste generation; inadequate management poses environmental and health hazards, regulatory non-compliance risk and reputational damage. Mitigation is partnering with government agencies for handling, recycling and disposal, adhering to e-waste regulations and regular monitoring of practices.
- Industry pricing / low ARPU and tariff dependence — Management states India has one of the lowest ARPUs in the world, making it challenging for telecom operators to sustain investment and innovation; the last tariff hike was in July 2024 after the prior increase in November 2021, so returns and the ability to fund next-generation network rollout depend on periodic tariff revision that is outside the Company's sole control.
- Export / international revenue exposure — BRSR Section A discloses that exports contribute 8% of the total turnover of the entity, a structural concentration disclosure - the balance of the business is domestic India-facing.

outlook.body: Stable outlook, indicating a positive outlook for the company's financial health
outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body:
- Execute the network investment programme - a planned capital investment of Rs 45,000 crore over FY27 to FY29 to expand a fully competitive network, with lender discussions ongoing to secure long-term funding
- Strengthen market competitiveness and translate a stronger balance sheet into sustained growth in customers and earnings; management frames FY26 as a year of resolution and FY27 as the beginning of a period of execution
- Resolve legacy financial overhangs and rebuild funding access - conclusion of the AGR matter, continued promoter support, stronger credit ratings and a return to positive subscriber additions as the platform for the next phase of growth
- Deepen enterprise capabilities through Vi Business - a dedicated enterprise corridor adding network capacity across data centres, a new IoT Innovation Lab, and planned deployment of smart metering solutions
- Expand AI-led digital and customer-service capabilities - ViNi voice assistant, an AI-based email bot, and Vi Protect for spam-call and malicious-domain blocking
- Drive consumer innovation and brand building - Non-Stop Hero 24x7 unlimited data, the REDX Family Plan extending unlimited data and international roaming to every family member, and the Chennai Super Kings communications partnership plus campaigns such as Vi 5G Fanfest, 1 Lakh Towers and Vi Number Rakshak
- Health, Safety and Wellbeing: the Company operates on the principle of 'not conducting business at the risk of people' and that 'everyone working for us returns home safely each day', reporting zero work-related fatalities during FY26 and major injuries at an all-time low, supported by Absolute Safety Rules, HSW standards and a governance framework covering operations and partner ecosystems.
- Climate governance: creation of a structured governance framework to oversee climate-change related issues and designation of a Sustainability/ESG committee to oversee climate risks, mitigation measures and contingency plans.
- Circularity and e-waste: partnering with relevant government agencies for proper handling, recycling and disposal of electronic waste, adhering to e-waste management regulations and regularly monitoring practices; the Company also reports continued circularity initiatives through material recovery, repair and reutilization across operations.
- Energy and emissions reduction levers: AI-enabled network optimization and continued deployment of energy-efficient infrastructure, together with renewable energy adoption, are cited as the routes to reduce environmental impact.
- Data privacy and cybersecurity: alignment of practices with the DPDP Act, regular customer privacy audits, minimised data retention, appropriate organizational and technical data-security measures, and cybersecurity/data-privacy practices aligned with globally recognised standards and certifications.
- People and diversity: voluntary attrition fell to a record low of 9.6% and diversity rose to 19.6% by March 31, 2026; average learning hours grew 45% in FY 2026 with a 90% adoption rate in future-fit skills such as Cloud and AI; women comprise 19.2% of permanent employees and 1 of 12 Board members (8.33%).
- People strategy for FY 2027: sharpen focus on deep domain expertise through Role-Based Functional Academies and scale the leadership pipeline via comprehensive Talent Development Journeys for high-potential cohorts, under the ABCDE strategic levers driving transformation toward FY 2030.
- Community grievance redress: mechanisms established across Vodafone Foundation-implemented programmes (including Connecting for Good and the Scholarship programme) allowing beneficiaries to raise concerns via email, chat, multi-lingual support, chatbot and social media with defined turnaround times. CSR under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 is stated as not applicable to the Company.
- Assurance: the BRSR disclosures carry reasonable assurance carried out by Emergent Ventures India Private Limited.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY26 marked a decisive acceleration in the Company's network investment cycle, described as the '17-5-5 Network Play'. Building on three-year investment contracts signed with Nokia, Ericsson and Samsung in September 2024, deployment stepped up meaningfully and the Company states it has deployed over Rs 16,000 Cr towards network investment over an 18-month period. It has further planned an investment of Rs 45,000 Cr between FY27 and FY29 to expand 4G coverage and 5G services, aimed at bridging the 4G coverage gap with competitors in 17 key circles that contribute over 99% of revenue; with these planned investments 4G population coverage in the 17 key circles is expected to increase to over 95%. In the remaining 5 circles the Company aims to bring 4G coverage to all national highways, key state highways, airports and places of tourist interest, and it aims to provide seamless 5G coverage to all urban areas. The total broadband site count increased to over 566,000 as of March 31, 2026 from over 494,500 in March 2025; 4G population coverage expanded by over 48 Mn to over 86% from about 83% in March 2025, while 4G data capacity increased by over 12% over the same period. The 5G rollout was initiated in March 2025 and, as of May 2026, 5G services are available in over 80 cities, deployed in key urban markets in a phased manner; the Company notes its latest 4G equipment is capable of being upgraded to 5G. On the enterprise side, a dedicated enterprise corridor added approximately 1.3 Tbps of network capacity across data centres, a new IoT Innovation Lab was set up, and the business plans to deploy 12 million smart metering solutions over the next three years. Funding for the programme is being pursued through ongoing discussions with lenders, alongside promoter support including a committed Aditya Birla Group equity infusion of US$500 million through fully convertible instruments.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India has one of the lowest ARPUs in the world; the last tariff hike was in July 2024 after the previous increase in November 2021, and management states an upward revision of tariff in future would drive a meaningful step-up in industry ARPU and strengthen the investment case for the sector
- Periodic tariff adjustments are described as essential if operators are to sustain investment and finance the rollout of next-generation networks
- Industry consolidation into three private operators and one state-owned player has restored pricing discipline and improved the sector's investment outlook
- Rural runway - rural tele-density at 60.46% versus urban at 151.47%, rural wireless subscribers at 546.60 Mn, and rural areas contributing 44% of the total internet subscriber base
- India's digital economy is projected to contribute nearly one-fifth of GDP by 2030, with India ranked third globally in digitalisation; telecom is positioned as the foundational infrastructure and critical enabler of the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision
- India is poised to become one of the largest mobile data traffic generating nations per active smartphone by 2030, requiring continued industry investment to keep pace with connectivity demand
- Government policy tailwinds - Union Budget FY26 allocation to the Department of Telecommunications and IT, a PLI scheme for telecom and networking products, a dedicated 6G Innovation Group, and draft National Telecom Policy 2025 targeting 100% 4G coverage and 90% 5G population coverage by 2030
- Company-level operating improvement - ARPU reached Rs 190 in the fourth quarter, up 8.3% year-on-year, and monthly subscriber additions turned positive from February 2026, the first sustained improvement in customer growth in several years
- Non-Stop Hero, the 24x7 unlimited data offering, recorded sequential growth of more than 25% for three consecutive quarters
- Macro backdrop - Indian GDP growth estimated at 7.7% in FY 2025-26 with RBI estimating 6.6% for FY 2026-27, and inflation expected to inch towards 5.1% on account of the energy shock and geopolitical tensions; the monsoon forecast remains a variable to watch
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Vodafone Idea Limited has received a credit rating upgrade from ICRA, with its long-term fund-based term loans revised to A- from BBB, and the outlook changed to Stable from Positive, indicating a positive outlook for the company's financial health. The upgrade reflects the company's improving operational and financial performance. However, the telecom sector remains competitive, and the company's ability to sustain its performance will be crucial.

verdicts.item: Management's gut feel is that the subscriber-loss trajectory should turn around by the end of FY25, driven by network investments, though no exact timeline can be given.

verdicts.item: Company remains actively engaged (CEO + promoters personally involved) to tie up debt funding for long-term network expansion; closure awaited pending clarity on AGR/government support (debt not contingent on AGR relief per TEV report).

verdicts.item: Company plans to take 4G tower count to ~215,000-220,000 (an increase of over 45,000 4G towers since start of investment cycle), with another 13,000 towers to be added by middle of Q1FY26.

currentContext.expansion: FY26 marked a decisive acceleration in the Company's network investment cycle, described as the '17-5-5 Network Play'. Building on three-year investment contracts signed with Nokia, Ericsson and Samsung in September 2024, deployment stepped up meaningfully and the Company states it has deployed over Rs 16,000 Cr towards network investment over an 18-month period. It has further planned an investment of Rs 45,000 Cr between FY27 and FY29 to expand 4G coverage and 5G services, aimed at bridging the 4G coverage gap with competitors in 17 key circles that contribute over 99% of revenue; with these planned investments 4G population coverage in the 17 key circles is expected to increase to over 95%. In the remaining 5 circles the Company aims to bring 4G coverage to all national highways, key state highways, airports and places of tourist interest, and it aims to provide seamless 5G coverage to all urban areas. The total broadband site count increased to over 566,000 as of March 31, 2026 from over 494,500 in March 2025; 4G population coverage expanded by over 48 Mn to over 86% from about 83% in March 2025, while 4G data capacity increased by over 12% over the same period. The 5G rollout was initiated in March 2025 and, as of May 2026, 5G services are available in over 80 cities, deployed in key urban markets in a phased manner; the Company notes its latest 4G equipment is capable of being upgraded to 5G. On the enterprise side, a dedicated enterprise corridor added approximately 1.3 Tbps of network capacity across data centres, a new IoT Innovation Lab was set up, and the business plans to deploy 12 million smart metering solutions over the next three years. Funding for the programme is being pursued through ongoing discussions with lenders, alongside promoter support including a committed Aditya Birla Group equity infusion of US$500 million through fully convertible instruments.

risks.note: BRSR material issue flagged as a Risk with negative financial implications. Rising privacy concerns over the use and sale of consumer data, heightened cybersecurity threats, and evolving Indian regulation under the DPDP Act. The Company states data security concerns can affect customer acquisition and retention, decrease market share and demand for VIL services, while data loss could cause non-compliance, legal ramifications and brand damage. Mitigations include licence-mandated confidentiality of subscriber information, alignment with DPDP Act requirements, regular customer privacy audits, minimised data retention and disciplinary action on breaches.

risks.risk: Quality of network infrastructure and pace of technology upgrade
risks.note: BRSR material issue flagged as a Risk with negative financial implications. Network infrastructure is vulnerable to technological failure from human error or natural disasters, and rapid technological advancement requires continuous upgrades to meet demand for stronger connectivity; failure to do so could adversely affect the business and market share. Mitigation is regular quality checks and recording complaint volumes. Scale of the service load is visible in the 4,770,473 customer complaints filed in FY 2025-26 with 7,961 pending at year close.

BRSR material issue flagged as a Risk. Failure to comply with regulatory requirements can lead to legal penalties, reputational damage and operational disruptions; the Company states it regularly monitors compliance to mitigate this and to build stakeholder trust.

BRSR material issue flagged as a Risk with negative financial implications. Emerging telecom-sector and global climate regulation (India's Net Zero 2070 commitment under UNFCCC/COP) focused on clean technologies and renewable energy, plus physical climate impacts on infrastructure - telecom disruptions threaten significant restructuring costs and hinder essential pre- and post-disaster communication. Mitigation is a structured climate governance framework and a designated Sustainability/ESG committee overseeing risks, mitigation and contingency plans.

BRSR material issue flagged as a Risk with negative financial implications. Telecom and networking equipment contributes significantly to e-waste generation; inadequate management poses environmental and health hazards, regulatory non-compliance risk and reputational damage. Mitigation is partnering with government agencies for handling, recycling and disposal, adhering to e-waste regulations and regular monitoring of practices.

risks.risk: Industry pricing / low ARPU and tariff dependence
risks.note: Management states India has one of the lowest ARPUs in the world, making it challenging for telecom operators to sustain investment and innovation; the last tariff hike was in July 2024 after the prior increase in November 2021, so returns and the ability to fund next-generation network rollout depend on periodic tariff revision that is outside the Company's sole control.
BRSR Section A discloses that exports contribute 8% of the total turnover of the entity, a structural concentration disclosure - the balance of the business is domestic India-facing.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India has one of the lowest ARPUs in the world; the last tariff hike was in July 2024 after the previous increase in November 2021, and management states an upward revision of tariff in future would drive a meaningful step-up in industry ARPU and strengthen the investment case for the sector
- Periodic tariff adjustments are described as essential if operators are to sustain investment and finance the rollout of next-generation networks
- Industry consolidation into three private operators and one state-owned player has restored pricing discipline and improved the sector's investment outlook
- Rural runway - rural tele-density at 60.46% versus urban at 151.47%, rural wireless subscribers at 546.60 Mn, and rural areas contributing 44% of the total internet subscriber base
- India's digital economy is projected to contribute nearly one-fifth of GDP by 2030, with India ranked third globally in digitalisation; telecom is positioned as the foundational infrastructure and critical enabler of the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision
- India is poised to become one of the largest mobile data traffic generating nations per active smartphone by 2030, requiring continued industry investment to keep pace with connectivity demand
- Government policy tailwinds - Union Budget FY26 allocation to the Department of Telecommunications and IT, a PLI scheme for telecom and networking products, a dedicated 6G Innovation Group, and draft National Telecom Policy 2025 targeting 100% 4G coverage and 90% 5G population coverage by 2030
- Company-level operating improvement - ARPU reached Rs 190 in the fourth quarter, up 8.3% year-on-year, and monthly subscriber additions turned positive from February 2026, the first sustained improvement in customer growth in several years
- Non-Stop Hero, the 24x7 unlimited data offering, recorded sequential growth of more than 25% for three consecutive quarters
- Macro backdrop - Indian GDP growth estimated at 7.7% in FY 2025-26 with RBI estimating 6.6% for FY 2026-27, and inflation expected to inch towards 5.1% on account of the energy shock and geopolitical tensions; the monsoon forecast remains a variable to watch

themes.title: Telecom & digital-infrastructure capex
themes.need: 5G monetization, FTTH and tower/fibre densification drive the connectivity cycle - and Q1FY27 repriced the optical leg outright. STLTECH booked order intake of INR 13,100cr in ONE quarter, 1.7x its entire FY26 order book, anchored by a multi-year $1.1bn hyperscaler deal running through FY29, taking the open order book to INR 18,618cr (up 2.4x QoQ) on revenue of INR 1,910cr (+87%) and EBITDA INR 397cr (+184%). It then raised guidance twice on the same call - EBITDA margin target from 20%-by-end-FY27 (already hit at 20.8% in Q1) to 23%, and Data-Center + Enterprise mix from 30% to 50% of FY27 revenue, after DC went from 1% of revenue in FY26 to 21%. The catch is supply, not demand: ex the anchor deal quarterly intake fell to ~INR 3,000cr from INR 7,000-8,000cr because 'we have to pick and choose the orders basis the capacity availability', with germanium and helium named as binding raw-material constraints. BHARTIARTL on ARPU + 5G; INDUSTOWER on tower rollout; SUYOG-tier on passive infra; GTPL/HFCL-tier on broadband + fibre; tariff hikes and rural FTTH are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler ramp against germanium/helium supply constraints and the raised 23% margin / 50% DC-mix guides; tariff-hike flow-through; 5G/FTTH capex; tower tenancy adds.
